story.head: Four points for Barron as the Blues beat the Golden Knights
paras: Aleksanteri Kaskimäki picked up his first NHL point. Pavel Buchnevich opened the scoring for the Blues on the power play midway through the first. Justin Barron scored his first goal for St. Louis less than four minutes later to make it 2-0. Brett Howden got the Golden Knights on the board early in the second, and Mason McTavish made it 3-1 for the Blues just under three minutes later. The third period was a wild one. Jack Eichel cut St. Louis’ lead to 3-2 early in the period, but they got no closer. Jimmy Snuggerud and Dylan Holloway scored just over two minutes apart midway through the period to stretch the lead to 5-2, and the Knights had no answer. Holloway scored his second of the night on the power play with just under four minutes left to make it 6-2. Barron finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Holloway added an assist for a three-point night.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Joel Hofer made 27 saves for the Blues, and Adin Hill allowed six goals on 31 shots.
Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Blues moved to 5-4-1, and the Golden Knights dropped to 8-4-0.
